Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:11:1.english: And what about there, where her betrothal is by Torah law - That she was betrothed with [her father's] consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:1:1.hebrew: שמא נתרצה הבן - בקידושין שקידש לו האב שלא מדעתו, לא אמרינן. דאב בקידושי בתו בכל דהו ניחא ליה — דטב למיתב טן דו — אבל גברא דייק ונסיב, ובן אינו ברשות אביו לקדש לו אשה שלא בשליחותו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:1:1.english: Perhaps the son consented - In [the case of] betrothal that the father betrothed for him without his knowledge, we do not say [this]. For a father, regarding the betrothal of his daughter, is pleased with anything — as 'it is better to dwell as two' — but a man is particular and [only then] marries; and a son is not in his father's authority for [the father] to betroth a woman to him without his agency.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:1:2.hebrew: ודילמא ארצויי ארצי - בן קמיה אביו, וגילה לו דעתו שהוא חפץ בה, והאב נעשה לו שליח מאליו, וזכין לאדם שלא בפניו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:1:2.english: And perhaps he made his desire known - The son [did so] before his father, and revealed to him his intention that he desires her, and the father became an agent for him of his own accord, and one can act in a person’s interest in his absence.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:1:4.hebrew: בפירוש - שמעתי ממנו דלא סבר ליה לדרב ושמואל, (דאין) חוששין שמא נתרצה האב, וכ"ש לשמא עשאו הבן שליח, אא"כ שמענו. ודקאמר אפילו למ"ד כו' — לרווחא דמילתא, כי היכי דלקבליה מיניה, קאמר הכי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:1:4.english: Explicitly - [Rabba bar Shimi meant:] I heard from him [Ravina] that he does not agree with Rav and Shmuel, [holding] (that we do not) suspect that perhaps the father consented, and all the more so [that we do not suspect] that perhaps the son made him an agent, unless we heard [him say so]. And [as for] that which [Ravina] said, "Even according to the one who says, etc.," he said this for the sake of expanding the argument, so that they would accept it from him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:2:1.hebrew: בכישא - אגודה. וקטנה שלא לדעת אביה הואי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:2:1.english: With a bundle - [That is,] a bundle. And she was a minor [betrothed] without her father's consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:3:1.english: Both this and that - With [even] one of them, it is degradation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:1.hebrew: הוא אמר לקריבי - מעשה היה שהאיש אמר לתת בתו קטנה לקרובו, ואשתו אמרה שיתננה לקרובה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:1.english: He said, "To my relative" - There was an incident where the man said [he wanted] to give his minor daughter to his relative, and his wife said that he should give her to her relative.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:2.hebrew: כפתיה - הכריחתו, והודה לה לתתה לקרובה. ועשו סעודה לחיבת חיתון, וזימנו את קרוביהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:2.english: She forced him - She coerced him, and he conceded to her to give her [the daughter] to her relative. And they made a feast out of affection for the marriage, and invited their relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:3.english: To the roof - In an upper chamber.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:4.hebrew: וקדשה - בסתר, ועדיין לא קבל האב קידושין מקרוב של אשתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:4:4.english: And betrothed her - In secret, and the father had not yet accepted betrothal from his wife's relative.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:5:1.hebrew: לא יעשו עולה - ולא חיישינן בהא שמא נתרצה האב, דלא הדר ביה מדבוריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:5:1.english: Shall not do iniquity - And we are not concerned in this [case] that perhaps the father consented, for he would not go back on his word.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:5:2.hebrew: רבא אמר - טעמא אחרינא, דודאי לא נתרצה: דכיון דטרח האי אבי הבת לעשות סעודה, אינו מפסידה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:5:2.english: Rava said - [This is] another reason that he certainly did not consent: for since this father of the daughter took the trouble to prepare a meal, he does not cause it to be lost.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:6:1.hebrew: דלא טרח - לעשות סעודה. לאביי, מכיון דאודי לה, תו לא הדר, ולא חיישינן לשמא נתרצה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:6:1.english: Where he did not take the trouble - To prepare a meal. According to Abaye, since he conceded to her, he does not go back [on his word], and we are not concerned that perhaps he consented [to the betrothal].

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:7:1.hebrew: אוכלת בתרומה - אם כהן הוא זה. ואע"פ שלא היתה חופה זו לדעת האב, ואמרו רבנן (כתובות דף נז:) "אין האשה אוכלת בתרומה עד שתכנס לחופה" — זו, הואיל וקידושיה לדעתו היו, חופה נמי ניחא ליה, עד שנשמע שיבא וימחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:7:1.english: She may partake of teruma - [This applies] if this [husband] is a priest. And even though this chupah was not with the father’s consent, and the Sages said (Ketubot 57b): “A woman does not partake of teruma until she enters the chupah” — [as for] this [woman], since her betrothal was with his consent, [the] chupah is also agreeable to him, until we hear that he comes and protests.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:8:1.hebrew: ומודה רב - אע"ג דגבי תרומה מחזקינן ליה בחזקה שנתרצה בחופה, התם הוא: דאי נימא לא נתרצה, אכלה מדאורייתא, דארוסה אוכלת בתרומה דבר תורה. אבל לענין ירושה, דבעינן שארו — מודה דאינו אלא כארוס, ואם מתה אינו יורשה, דכיון דמספקא לן אם מתרצה בחופה או לאו, אוקימנא ממונא בחזקת מריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:8:1.english: And Rav concedes - Even though regarding teruma we maintain the presumption that [the father] consented to the chuppah, that is [only] there: for [even] if we say that he did not consent, she may eat by Torah law, as a betrothed woman [arusah] eats teruma by Torah law. But regarding inheritance, where we require [her to be] “his kin” [she’ero, i.e., fully married] — [Rav] concedes that he is merely like a betrothed husband [arus], and if she dies he does not inherit from her; for since we are in doubt whether [the father] consents to the chuppah or not, we establish the money in the possession of its owner.

Rashi on Kiddushin 45b:9:1.english: And she married without [his] consent - She did not inform him.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:7:1.hebrew: בפירוש אמר מר לא סבירא ליה להא דשמואל - דקאמר לעיל: "חיישינן שמא נתרצה לראשון". ופירש בקונטרס, דהיינו רבינא דלא סבר לדשמואל. ואע"ג דקאמר רבינא: "אפי' למ"ד דחיישינן שמא נתרצה האב", לאו משום דס"ל הכי, אלא לרווחא דמילתא נקטיה. ופסק רב אלפס ובשאלתות דרב אחאי דהילכתא כרבינא, דהוא בתראה וסוף הוראה היה, ורבה בר שימי נמי סבר כוותיה; ולא חיישינן שמא נתרצה האב, ואין צריך לא גט ולא מיאון, ואפי' שידכו. ואע"ג דמתמה גמרא לעיל (קידושין דף מד:): "ואע"ג דשידכו?" — מיהו איכא דאמרי אינו סובר כן. וא"כ, אין צריך לדחוק ולפרש מה שפי' ר"י לעיל: "אפילו מיאון אינה צריכה" — דוקא היכא דלא שידכו; דאיכא למימר כמו שפי' בקונטרס, ומיירי אפילו שידכו. ואי משום דמתמה גמרא: "ואע"ג דשידכו?", איכא למימר דמאיכא דאמרי ואילך אית ליה סברא אחרת, ומסתמא זו היא: דאפילו בשידכו אינה צריכה מיאון, שהרי כמו כן קאמר רבינא. ועוד פסק בשאלתות דרב אחאי, בקטנה שהלך אביה למדינת הים, שהיא יכולה להתקדש מדרבנן כדין יתומה דאין לה אב — דתקנו רבנן קידושין משום הפקר; וזו שהלך אביה למד"ה, הרי היא כיתומה משום הפקר. וה"ר מנחם מיונ"י אינו מודה בדבר. ומעשה אירע באחד שהלך לארץ רחוקה ולו בת קטנה, ונתקדשה הבת, ואסר ה"ר מנחם מיונ"י לקיימה, ואמר: "חיישינן שמא יקדשנה אביה לאיש אחר במקום שהוא, ונמצא בא זה עליה באיסור אשת איש". ושלח לו רבינו תם: "לדבריך, אם מת האב במד"ה, היא תאסר לכל אדם לעולם, שמא קידשה אביה במדינת הים ואין אנו יודעים למי!". והשיב רבינו מנחם: "דלהא לא חיישינן; 'שמא יקדש' אמרי', 'שמא קידש' לא אמרינן — דכי האי גוונא אמר פרק כל הגט (גיטין דף כח:): 'לשמא מת לא חיישי', לשמא ימות — תנאי היא, וקי"ל כרבי יוסי דפליג עליה דר"מ דאמר חיישינן לשמא ימות, דר"מ ור' יוסי הלכה כר' יוסי'". ועל זה אמר ר"ת: דהשתא דאתית להכי, אף כשהיא קטנה מותרת; דכיון דלא חיישי' שמא קידש, א"כ היא מותרת לעולם, דכל שעה ושעה יש לנו לומר דעדיין לא קידש; ואפי' חיישת שמא יקדש, הואיל וכל שעה יש לומר עדיין לא קידש — מותרת היא אצלו. ולא דמי לשמא ימות — דהתם מיירי שאסר את אשתו בתרומה כשהגט חל שעה אחת לפני מיתתו, ואיכא למימר דמיד ימות, נמצא דכל שעה אסורה לאכול בתרומה, דאיכא למימר דמיד ימות; אבל הכא, דאינה אסורה עד שיחולו הקידושין שקידש אביה שם, כל שעה איכא למימר עדיין לא חלו הקידושין, כדפי'. והביא ר"ת ראיה מהלכות גדולות שפירש בהלכות קידושין: "קטנה דאיתא לאבוה במדינת הים, ואנסיבתא אמה — שאלתא הדא מלתא קמיה דרבנן, ואמרו: שפיר עבדת אמה, דנישואין תקינו לקטנה; אם איתיה לאב מקדשה קידושין מן התורה, ואי ליתיה מינסבא בתיקון חכמים, ולכי גדלה גדלי נישואין בהדה, ולכי אתי אב לא צריך לקדשה":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:7:1.english: "The Master explicitly said that he does not hold in accordance with this [statement] of Shmuel" - For [Shmuel] said above (44b): "We are concerned that perhaps [the father] consented to the first [betrothal]." And Rashi explained that this refers to Ravina, who does not hold in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel. And even though Ravina said: "Even according to the one who says that we are concerned that perhaps the father consented," [this was] not because he holds so, but rather he stated it as an added concession [to widen the argument]. And Rav Alfas [the Rif] and the She'iltot of Rav Achai ruled that the halakha is in accordance with Ravina, as he was a later authority [batra'ei] and was at the end of [the era of Talmudic] instruction, and Rabba bar Shimi also holds like him; and [therefore] we are not concerned that perhaps the father consented, and she requires neither a bill of divorce nor refusal [mi'un], even if they had arranged a match. And even though the Gemara above (Kiddushin 44b) asks in astonishment: "Even if they arranged a match?!" — nevertheless, [the version introduced by] "there are those who say" [ika de'amrei] does not hold so. And if so, there is no need to exert [oneself] to explain as the Ri explained above, that "she does not even require refusal" is specifically where they did not arrange a match; for one can say as Rashi explained, that it deals with [a case where] they even arranged a match. And if [one objects] because the Gemara asks in astonishment: "Even if they arranged a match?!", one can say that from [the version of] "there are those who say" onward, it maintains a different line of reasoning, and presumably this is it: that even where they arranged a match she does not require refusal, for Ravina likewise says so. And furthermore, [it is] ruled in the She'iltot of Rav Achai regarding a minor girl whose father went overseas, that she can become betrothed rabbinically according to the law of an orphan who has no father, for the Rabbis instituted betrothal [for an orphan girl] so that people would not treat her as ownerless property; and this [girl] whose father went overseas is like an orphan so that people would not treat her as ownerless property. And Rabbi Menachem of Joigny does not concede to this matter. And an incident occurred involving a certain man who went to a distant land and had a minor daughter, and the daughter became betrothed, and Rabbi Menachem of Joigny forbade [her husband] to remain married to her, and said: "We are concerned that perhaps her father will betroth her to another man in the place where he is, and this [husband] will turn out to be cohabiting with her under the prohibition of a married woman." And Rabbeinu Tam sent [a challenge] to him: "According to your words, if the father dies overseas, she should be forbidden to any man forever, lest her father betrothed her overseas and we do not know to whom!" And Rabbeinu Menachem replied: "Concerning this we are not concerned; we say 'perhaps he will betroth,' [but] we do not say 'perhaps he [already] betrothed.' For [in] a case like this, [the Gemara] said in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 28b): 'We are not concerned that perhaps he died; [as for whether we are concerned] that perhaps he will die, it is [a dispute between] Tannaim, and we establish the halakha in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who disagrees with Rabbi Meir who said: We are concerned that perhaps he will die — for [in a dispute between] Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei, the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.'" And regarding this Rabbeinu Tam said: "Now that you have arrived at this [reasoning], even while she is a minor she is permitted! For since we are not concerned that perhaps he [already] betrothed [her], if so, she is permitted forever, because at each and every moment we can say that he has not yet betrothed [her]; and even if you are concerned that perhaps he will betroth [her in the future], since at every moment it can be said that he has not yet betrothed [her], she is permitted to him. And it is not comparable to 'perhaps he will die,' for there it deals with [a case where a priest] forbade his wife from [eating] teruma where the bill of divorce takes effect one hour before his death, and it can be said that he will die immediately, so it turns out that at every moment she is forbidden to eat teruma, since it can be said that he will die immediately; but here, where she is not forbidden until the betrothal that her father performed there takes effect, at every moment it can be said: 'The betrothal has not yet taken effect,' as explained." And Rabbeinu Tam brought a proof from the Halakhot Gedolot, who explained in Hilkhot Kiddushin: "A minor girl whose father is overseas and her mother married her off: this matter was asked before the Rabbis, and they said: Her mother acted properly, for they instituted marriage for a minor girl: if the father is present, he betroths her with a betrothal of Torah law, and if he is not present, she is married by the enactment of the Sages; and when she grows up, the marriage grows up with her, and when the father comes, he does not need to betroth her."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:7:2.hebrew: ונמצאת זרה למפרע - נראה דזרה דנקט לא קאמר שתהא זרה דאורייתא, שהרי מן התורה ארוסה אוכלת בתרומה, אלא זרה דרבנן קאמר. ואע"ג דלא שייך הכא לא משום סימפון ולא משום שמא ימזגו — דכיון דנכנסת לחופה, דוכתא מייחד לה ומבדק בדיק לה — אפ"ה לא חילקו חכמים בין ארוסה לארוסה; כלומר: כיון שאין חופתה חופה גמורה, שהאב יכול למחות, לא פלוג רבנן בין זו ללא נכנסה לחופה כלל:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:7:2.english: "And she will be found [to be] a non-priest retroactively" - It appears that in mentioning "a non-priest," he does not mean that she would be a non-priest by Torah law, for by Torah law a betrothed woman [arusah] eats teruma; rather, he means a rabbinic "non-priest." And even though neither [the concern] on account of a defect [simpon] nor [the concern] on account of "lest they pour [a cup of teruma for her in her father's house]" applies here — for since she entered the chuppah, he designates a place for her and inspects her — even so, the Sages did not distinguish between [one] betrothed woman and [another] betrothed woman; that is to say, since her chuppah is not a complete chuppah, as the father can protest, the Rabbis did not distinguish between this [woman] and [one who] did not enter the chuppah at all.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:7:3.hebrew: הוה עובדא וחש לה רב להא דרב אסי - נראה דהלכה כרב אסי, דהא הדר ביה רב. אך ר"ת פסק הילכתא כרב, שהרי רב אסי היה תלמידו; ובכל מקום שהרב והתלמיד חולקין הלכה כדברי הרב באמוראי ראשונים, עד אביי ורבא. אבל מכאן ואילך פסקינן כבתראי, לפי שדקדקו יותר מן הראשונים להעמיד הלכה על בוריה. ואע"ג דחש לה רב להא דרב אסי, מש"ה לא חזר בו, אלא חומרא בעלמא שהחמיר אנפשיה; כמו שמצינו בפ"ק דמגילה (דף ה.): "אמר רב: מגילה בזמנה ביחיד, שלא בזמנה בעשרה. רב אסי אמר: אחד זה ואחד זה בעשרה. הוה עובדא וחש לה רב להא דרב אסי". ואפ"ה קי"ל כרב, דהא ר' יוחנן קאי כוותיה בפ"ב דמגילה (דף יט:), דאמר ר' חייא בר אבא אמר ר' יוחנן: "הקורא במגילה הכתובה בין הכתובים לא יצא", ומחו ליה אמוחיה: "לא שנו אלא בצבור מפני כבוד צבור, אבל יחיד לא" — אלמא משמע דפעמים קורין אותה ביחיד, והיינו בזמנה כרב:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:7:3.english: "There was an incident, and Rav was concerned for this [ruling] of Rav Asi" - It appears that the halakhah is in accordance with Rav Asi, since Rav retracted [his position]. However, Rabbeinu Tam ruled that the halakhah is like Rav, for Rav Asi was his disciple; and wherever the master and the disciple disagree, the halakhah is in accordance with the words of the master among the early Amoraim, up to Abaye and Rava. But from that point forward we rule in accordance with the later authorities (halakhah ke-vatrai), because they were more meticulous than the early authorities in establishing the halakhah with precision. And even though Rav was concerned for this [ruling] of Rav Asi, he did not retract [his view] on account of this; rather, it was merely a stringency that he adopted for himself. This is just as we find in the first chapter of Megillah (5a): "Rav said: [Reading the] Megillah at its designated time [may be done] by an individual; not at its designated time, [it must be] with ten. Rav Asi said: Both this and that [must be] with ten. There was an incident, and Rav was concerned for this [ruling] of Rav Asi." And even so, we hold in accordance with Rav, for Rabbi Yochanan stands in agreement with him in the second chapter of Megillah (19b), as Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said: "One who reads from a Megillah that is written among the Writings [Ketuvim] has not fulfilled his obligation." And they struck him on the head [i.e., vehemently rejected this]: "They taught this only in a congregation, on account of the honor of the congregation, but [for] an individual, no [it is valid]." Consequently, this implies that at times it is read by an individual, and that is at its designated time, in accordance with Rav.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:8:1.hebrew: אוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה - ואפי' הוא מוחזק בנכסי מלוג שלה, אינו בחזקתו אלא בחזקת יורשי האשה, דתפיסתו שלא כדין היתה. ואע"ג דשרי לה רב לאכול בתרומה — היינו משום דמן התורה ארוסה בת ישראל אוכלת בתרומה, כדפירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 45b:8:1.english: "Establish money in the possession of its owner" - And even if he is in possession of her usufruct property [nikhsei melog], it is not [considered to be] in his possession, but rather in the possession of the woman's heirs, for his seizure was unlawful. And even though Rav permitted her to partake of teruma — that is because by Torah law, a betrothed Israelite woman may partake of teruma, as Rashi explained.
